language.heading: Language
language.desc: Choose the display language for PoolRouter. This choice is saved to your account and applies on all your devices.
language.apply_note: The display changes as soon as you choose.
language.scope_note: What gets translated: menus, labels, and on-screen messages. Dates, times, and numbers follow the chosen language; the time zone stays WIB. Data you enter, such as provider and pool names, is not translated.

page.title: Providers
page.subtitle: A provider is a third-party API that PoolRouter calls, such as the Dukcapil API.

empty.title: No providers yet
empty.body: Add a provider to start receiving requests from client applications. First, set up the secrets (USER_ID, PASSWORD, IP_USER) under Secrets.

template.label: Body template (JSON)
template.help: Write keys exactly as in the Dukcapil document, including the spelling TRESHOLD.

error.alert: The template can't be saved yet. Line {{nomor_baris}}: {{rincian}}
error.brace_missing: a closing curly brace is missing.
error.secret_missing: Secret {{nama}} hasn't been created yet. Create it under Secrets, then save the template again.

auth.label: Authentication
auth.help: Available in F0: credentials in body, API key in header, or none. JWT/OIDC comes in F2.

schema.label: Response schema (JSON)
schema.help: Output to the client: status and score for each element sent. Elements that weren't sent don't appear.

rules.info: A new rule applies to new requests only. Requests already queued use the rule that was in force when they entered the queue.
rules.type_help: Options: Regex, Enum, Length, Date format. Custom validation functions aren't available in F0.
rules.no_defaults: Rule values stay empty until BGN sets them (K-06). The system doesn't fill in defaults.
rules.no_custom: Custom validation functions aren't available in this version yet.

endpoint.info: Only a platform admin can change this value. Every change is recorded in the audit log (who, when, what).
endpoint.threshold_help: Sent to Dukcapil from here. Clients must not send TRESHOLD (rejected with 422).

page.title: Secrets
page.subtitle: Secret values are stored masked. Once saved, a value can't be viewed or copied; it can only be replaced.
page.write_only: The value is masked. Once saved, it can't be viewed or copied.

replace.title: Replace secret {{nama}}
replace.body: The old value can't be viewed. The new value replaces it right away.

blocked.title: Secret is still in use
blocked.body: {{nama}} is still used by active providers: {{daftar}}. Deactivate or change those providers first, then delete this secret.

empty.title: No secrets yet
empty.body: A secret stores a provider credential, such as USER_ID and PASSWORD. Add a secret before you create a provider template.

daily_quota.help: Counted per day according to the reset time (reset time setting to follow).

sync_share.help: When sync traffic is low, async may use the remainder. Sync above the share is rejected with 429.

empty.title: No upstream pools yet
empty.body: Add an upstream pool to set the daily quota and hourly rate limit for a provider.

page.subtitle: Applies to async requests. Sync requests aren't randomized or delayed, but they still count toward the quota.
page.delay_help: A random delay between sends is picked between the minimum and the maximum.
page.adjacent_help: Maximum share of consecutive NIKs that may be sent next to each other.
page.warn: A delay that is too long can keep the rate limit of {{batas, number}}/hour from being reached. Check the load-test results before changing it.

page.title: Downstream pools
page.subtitle: Each downstream pool is linked to one upstream pool (single allocation). Reserved/shareable allocation and priority come in F1.
page.ttl_help: Leave empty for 24 hours. Changes apply to new requests only.

empty.title: No downstream pools yet
empty.body: Add a downstream pool and link it to one upstream pool.

page.title: Metadata contract
page.info: Metadata is recorded in the transaction log for feedback data. It isn't sent to Dukcapil.
page.note: A request without a required field is rejected before it uses quota. Adding an optional field doesn't make older requests fail. The final field list follows once the data contract is agreed.

empty.title: No fields yet
empty.body: Add a metadata field to record it in the transaction log.

form.title: Add client
form.intro: A client is a BGN application that calls PoolRouter.
form.name: Client name
form.name_help: A unique name, for example the application name.
form.pool_help: A client can only use the pool it is linked to.

empty.title: No clients yet
empty.body: Add a client for each application that will call PoolRouter.

dialog.body: Copy the secret now. It is shown only once and can't be viewed again after you close this dialog.

address.help: Must start with https://. Addresses without https are rejected.
address.error: The webhook address must start with https://.

secret.heading: Signing secret
secret.desc: Created by the system and shown only once. Install it in your application to verify webhooks.

rotate.title: Rotate webhook secret?
rotate.body: The old secret stops working immediately. The {{nama_client}} application will fail to verify webhooks until the new secret is installed in it.

failures.heading: Delivery failures
failures.alert_one: {{count, number}} webhook failed in the last 24 hours. A webhook is sent once; you can still fetch the result by polling with queue_id.
failures.alert_other: {{count, number}} webhooks failed in the last 24 hours. A webhook is sent once; you can still fetch the result by polling with queue_id.

empty.no_failures: No failures in the last 24 hours.

page.sync_used: Sync used {{terpakai, number}} of the {{persen, number}}% limit
page.note: Figures are counted from attempts to Dukcapil, including retries and failed calls. Differences from the transaction log can occur.

filter.code_help: Find a record using its transaction code.

page.export_help: Enter a valid 16-digit NIK to enable export.

payload.help: Filled in from the search reason. You can edit it.

pool.title: Deactivate upstream pool?
pool.scope: Waiting requests in this pool are affected.
pool.new_requests: New requests to this pool are rejected with code 503.

upstream.scope: Only requests that have already been routed to this pool are stopped, as counted below. Requests that have not been routed are not cancelled.
upstream.timing_window: During those 30 seconds, sync requests that were already accepted can still be processed. Async requests that were routed to this pool are stopped without a call to the provider: cancelled, or failed if waiting for a retry. Requests that have not been routed keep waiting, then are processed through an active upstream pool or end as expired once their TTL runs out. Neither group is counted above or recorded in the action audit.
upstream.cancelled_one: {{count, number}} request that has been routed to this pool but not yet tried will be cancelled. It has never been sent to the provider and uses no quota.
upstream.cancelled_other: {{count, number}} requests that have been routed to this pool but not yet tried will be cancelled. They have never been sent to the provider and use no quota.
upstream.body_zero: No requests have been routed to this pool.
upstream.new_requests_rerouted: No later than 30 seconds after you confirm, new requests from the downstream pools that use this pool are no longer routed to this pool and are served by another active upstream pool.
upstream.last_active: This is the last active upstream pool for at least one downstream pool. New requests to those downstream pools are rejected with code 503, no later than 30 seconds after you confirm.
upstream.last_active_waiting: Waiting requests that have not been routed to this pool are not cancelled. They stay queued, the client can still cancel them, and they are processed as usual if an active upstream pool exists for their downstream pool before their TTL runs out. If none exists, they end as expired.
upstream.last_active_stop: To stop waiting requests, deactivate the downstream pool.
upstream.unused: This pool is not used by any downstream pool, so no new requests are affected.

provider.title: Deactivate provider?
provider.scope: All waiting requests in every upstream pool that uses this provider are affected, from any downstream pool. The active status of the pools does not change.
provider.new_requests: New requests that use this provider are rejected with code 503.
provider.recover: The route recovers as soon as the provider is activated again.

endpoint.title: Deactivate endpoint?
endpoint.new_requests: New requests to this endpoint are rejected with code 403. Clients must not retry them.

client.title: Deactivate client?
client.scope: All requests that belong to this client are affected.
client.new_requests: New requests from this client are rejected with code 401.
client.in_flight_result: The result of a request that is being processed is sent by webhook if the client webhook is active. A deactivated client cannot fetch results by polling (401). If the client is activated again before the result TTL of the downstream pool runs out, a completed result can be fetched again.
client.webhook_stays: Webhooks are still sent to this client while its webhook is active. To stop them, deactivate the client webhook separately.

credential.title: Revoke credential?
credential.scope: Only requests that came in through this credential are affected. Other credentials of the same client keep working; revoking one credential does not stop the client.
credential.new_requests: New requests with this credential are rejected with code 401, without waiting for the token to expire.
credential.in_flight_result: The result of a request that is being processed can be fetched with another credential of this client.
credential.irreversible: Revoking cannot be undone. A revoked credential cannot be activated again (the system rejects it with 409). To replace it, create a new credential; a client can have at most 2 active credentials.

common.cancelled_one: {{count, number}} waiting request will be cancelled. It has never been sent to the provider and uses no quota.
common.cancelled_other: {{count, number}} waiting requests will be cancelled. They have never been sent to the provider and use no quota.
common.failed_one: {{count, number}} request waiting for a retry will be marked failed and won't be tried again. Quota already used and earlier attempt logs stay as they are, with no quota refund.
common.failed_other: {{count, number}} requests waiting for a retry will be marked failed and won't be tried again. Quota already used and earlier attempt logs stay as they are, with no quota refund.
common.estimate_note: These numbers are estimates. The final numbers appear in the result of the action and in the audit.
common.in_flight_one: For information only: {{count, number}} request is being processed and is not counted above. The attempt in progress is allowed to finish. If it fails temporarily, the request is not tried again and ends as failed.
common.in_flight_other: For information only: {{count, number}} requests are being processed and are not counted above. The attempts in progress are allowed to finish. If one fails temporarily, it is not tried again and ends as failed.
common.timing: New requests are rejected no later than 30 seconds after you confirm.
common.timing_window: During those 30 seconds, sync requests that were already accepted can still be processed. Async requests that get through are cancelled and not sent to the provider.
common.reversible: A platform admin can activate it again in the Web UI. Activation only applies to new requests. Requests that were cancelled or failed do not come back; the client must send a new request.
common.webhook: Clients whose webhook is active receive one webhook for each request that becomes cancelled or failed, with the status and the reason. A webhook is not sent again if delivery fails.
common.audit: This action is recorded in the configuration audit: who, when, and the old and new values.
common.action_failed: The action did not succeed. Try again.
